facts.text: Founded in 1905 along a now-abandoned Northern Pacific Railway branch from Carrington to Turtle Lake, Mercer grew with the early 20‑century railroad boom.
The name comes from William Henry Harrison Mercer, a well‑known rancher in the Missouri River Valley for many years and for whom Mercer County is also named.
Zion Lutheran Cemetery, a National Register site, showcases unique 19th‑ and early 20th‑century wrought‑iron crosses that reflect the area's German‑Russian heritage.
Mercer's flat to undulating terrain, formed by glacial deposits, offers fertile loess soils perfect for wheat and sunflower farming.
The community adopted the motto 'Bringing Home the Bison' to evoke its connection to North Dakota's wildlife and open prairies.
